title: Senate gearing up to investigate Ukraine’s access to Starshield - Breaking Defense
html:
HALIFAX, Nova Scotia — As Democrats prepare to run both chambers of the US Congress next year, a prominent democratic senator is vowing that one of the first orders of business will be looking at what crippled Ukraine’s access to SpaceX’s Starshield.

“Look at Starshield being turned on and off. … It is killing civilians. It is undermining the world’s confidence in the United States as a supplier of key security equipment,” Sen. Chris Coons of Delaware told an audience here Friday. “Those are services paid for by American taxpayers under contract. This is not Elon Musk’s personal toy.”

Ukraine has relied on SpaceX’s Starshield — the US military variant of the Starlink satellite network — for drone operations against Russian threats and targets. In October, Ukrainian officials claimed a sudden change to the Starshield network, which they directly attributed to the failure of drones and defenses that led to military and civilian deaths. Officials from the Eastern European country later said service had been fully restored later in October before asserting this month it was again hampered.

“We experience speed limitations as of now on Ukrainian occupied territories and across the contact line,” Ukraine’s Chargé d’Affaires Denys Sienik said in a Nov. 9 statement to Breaking Defense. “The contact line is the first line of our defence and the first point for interception of Russian drones. It started gradually several days ago and now the speed limitations of 100 mph are in place in those areas.”

Sienik added that Kyiv still did not have clarity from the Pentagon or SpaceX over the cause of the slow down or who may have ordered it. The US Embassy did not respond to questions about the status of Starshield at the time.

Coons has vowed to get some answers and is in a position to do that as a senior Democrat on the Senate Appropriations defense subcommittee and top contender to take the gavel as chairman of the Foreign Relations Committee.

If he secures that leadership post, he vowed for one of the first hearings to be examining the Ukraine-Starshield issue to find out: “What the hell is happening? Why is this being done? What are the consequences and the costs? And what does it say about our reliability in the future?” he said.

Coons is not the only lawmaker asking questions, given that the reported slowdown coincided with US President Donald Trump announcing he had reached a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel to help lower the cost of fuel, while also warning Ukraine not to strike Russian refineries.

CNN reported this week that Democratic Rep. Jim Himes, who is expected to become chairman of the House Intelligence Committee, sent a classified communication to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton demanding clarity on what led to the slowdown of Ukraine’s Starshield.

The microscope on SpaceX is part of a larger push by Democrats to investigate possible incidents of corruption inside the Trump administration. Here, Coons asked an international audience of defense ministers and other foreign leaders to be patient.
While Congress holds the power of the purse, he warned that the Office of Management and Budget has the ability to move money around and hamper attempts to support Ukraine or cut off funding for the ongoing war with Iran. 

“We will see change. It will not be as swift, as complete, or as easy as I think our pundits on television [think],” Coons added.
summary: Senators want to know why access was restricted, at what cost, and what it says about US reliability as a partner.
